correctness.rationale: The unilateral material increment is alpha(r/n-1); minimizing the strictly convex opinion loss at y_i=c z_i+d x_i gives an optimized action difference K(z_i-1/2-eta). For two members of one community, z_i-z_j=-a(y_i-y_j)/(m-1) and (1+ca/(m-1))(y_i-y_j)=d(x_i-x_j). A cooperator would have weakly lower z than a defector in the same community, incompatible with strict cooperation and either strict or tie-selected defection, including a=0. Thus each block is constant. The block sum and difference equations give y_A+y_B=x_A+x_B and y_A-y_B=d(x_A-x_B)/(1-c(2a-1)). For a polarized pair only the cooperator threshold can bind: h d/[2(1-ch)]>eta, h=2a-1, is equivalent to the stated a>a_c and is feasible only at eta<1/2. The consensus means 0 and 1 give the other two cases. Defectors are strict in every surviving tie-selected block profile, so fixed points and strict Nash equilibria agree. Critical equalities give weak, not strict, cooperation.
residual_risks: Not a classification of ordinary weak equilibria. For instance n=6, a=0, r=2, alpha=1/17, beta=lambda=8/17 permits two cooperators at opinion 5/6 and one defector at opinion 1/3 in each block, with common z=2/3=1/2+eta and every action tied. This profile is not a fixed point under defection at ties.
The 864 exact cases and 96,768 profiles reported in the supplied verification are author checks, not independent or all-parameter evidence.
